item.title: Wall Street Week | Venezuela’s Oil Test, Overcapacity in Renewables, Defense Tech Boom
item.description: This week, while Venezuela has the oil reserves to impact global energy markets, rebuilding production will take years, billions of dollars and investor trust. And, Europe’s solar success is creating growing pains for investors, generators and power markets. Plus, can data centers turn Scotland’s wasted wind into an AI advantage? Later, a more dangerous world is pushing the Pentagon and Silicon Valley closer together, creating a new boom in defense and space technologies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former NY Fed President on Remembering 9/11
item.description: William Dudley discussed Dudley’s experience on a diverted flight during the FAA ground stop after the attacks. Dudley said the plane was unable to land in the U.S. and was sent to Saint John’s, Newfoundland, where passengers were kept for six days. He compared the experience to the musical Come From Away, saying it accurately captured what stranded travelers went through. Dudley recalled the uncertainty at first, including the pilot’s refusal to explain what was happening until they were on the ground, but emphasized the generosity of Canadians who housed, fed, and clothed the stranded passengers. The conversation also reflected on the tragedy of Sept. 11, honoring first responders and noting that, despite the horror of the attacks, many people rose to the occasion with heroism and kindness. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: KBW CEO on re-building Manhattan after 9/11
item.description: Tom Michaud describes how KBW responded in the aftermath of Sept. 11 by focusing first on helping the families of victims and then on rebuilding the firm. He says he, John Duffy, and Andy Senczak formed the top leadership group, alongside an office of the chairman, and that nearly all of the firm’s colleagues came from the equity side. Michaud says the rebuilding effort gave the team a way to channel grief and energy into action, and he recalls the determination that KBW could not end because of the attacks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former NYC Deputy Mayor on Remembering 9/11
item.description: Edward Skyler reflects on the aftermath of 9/11, saying it was extremely difficult to make decisions in the wake of a tragedy that left 2,700 people murdered and the city filled with grief, anxiety, and political tension. He recalls that when Mayor Bloomberg was sworn in on 01/01/2002, smoke was still rising from the World Trade Center site and the economic damage had already been done. Skyler says the period was marked by intense emotions and strong voices from people opposed to New York, and that the job of city leaders was to listen to all sides and develop a plan that served the city’s best interests, even if it disappointed some people. He concludes that, in hindsight, those decisions have stood the test of time. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rebuilding After 9/11, Cantor Fitzgerald's Annual Charity, Eye on Energy Markets
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Former NY Fed President, Bill Dudley. Tom Michaud KBW CEO. Ed Skyler Former NYC Deputy Mayor. Matt DiLiberto, SL Green CFO. Ed Morse Hartree Partners Senior Advisor And Commodities analyst, Brandon Lutnick, Cantor Fitzgerald Chariman and Kyle Lutnick Cantor Fitzgerald Vice Chariman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SL Green CFO on Lower Manhattan's rebound after 9/11
item.description: Matt DiLiberto discussed the 25-year transformation of Lower Manhattan after Sept. 11, saying the area has been “reimagined” from a largely nine-to-five financial district into a vibrant neighborhood where people live, work, study, and visit. He said the central question after the attacks was not whether the area would be rebuilt, but how, how long it would take, who would do it, and what it would ultimately look like. DiLiberto pointed to the area’s growth in population and housing, along with a mix of office space and memorialization around the World Trade Center site. From SL Green’s perspective, he said the company focused more on residential projects in the area because of how the neighborhood evolved, citing developments such as 100 Church Street, 33 Beekman, and 180 Broadway. He framed the redevelopment as part of a broader need for New York to remain strong and vibrant not just in Midtown, but downtown as well. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JD.com Unit Agrees to Pay SEC $500,000 Over ‘Sham Transactions’
item.description: A unit of China’s online retailer JD.com Inc. agreed to pay $500,000 to settle US Securities and Exchange Commission claims it made a series of “sham transactions” to meet revenue targets for several quarters starting in October 2022.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Bond Trader Whose Wrong-Way Bets Collapsed Firm Gets 16 Years
item.description: A former trader at IFS Securities Inc. was ordered to serve more than 16 years in prison for unauthorized bond trades in 2019 that led to $30 million in losses and bankrupted the Chicago broker-dealer.
item.dc:creator: Steve Stroth

item.title: KKR Wraps Up $2.1 Billion Leveraged Loan for Integer Acquisition
item.description: KKR & Co. Inc. finalized a $2.1 billion loan to help fund its pending acquisition of medical-device maker Integer Holdings Corp. after securing more-favorable terms, seizing on investor demand for leveraged-buyout financings.
item.dc:creator: Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Jon Ledecky reflects on Sept. 11 and NYC sports scene
item.description: Jon Ledecky, NHL team New York Islanders co-owner, sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to remember the events on Sept. 11, the power of sports and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Finding Stability in Investing: Masters in Business with Seth Bernstein
item.description: Barry speaks with Seth Bernstein, Chief Executive Officer of AllianceBernstein. They discuss his tenure at JPMorgan Chase where he was managing director and global head of Managed Solutions & Strategy at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. They discuss understanding the Private Credit industry and the future of Mutual Funds as ETFs become the future of investing. Seth also discusses the importance of in-person collaboration as well as how to invest for retirement. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bill Dudley Expects Fed to Raise Rate by 25 Bps
item.description: Bill Dudley, a Bloomberg Opinion columnist and former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, says he would be shocked if the Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates by 25 basis points at their next meeting. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan’s GPIF May Sell $62 Billion of Treasuries, Santander Says
item.description: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund could sell as much as $62 billion of US Treasuries without a formal revamp of its asset-allocation policy, according to analysts at Banco Santander SA.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie

item.title: AI-Obsessed Wall Street Pours Billions Into Inflation-Era Bets
item.description: The list of challenges confronting Wall Street piled up this week. Oil firmly above $100. Inflation refusing to disappear. A defiant bond market that all but dared Scott Bessent to bring more policy firepower.
item.dc:creator: Vildana Hajric and Isabelle Lee

item.title: CFTC Clears Faster Payouts for Tipster Awards Under $5 Million
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission plans to automatically award successful whistleblowers 30% of any enforcement penalties collected if a tipster is due to receive $5 million or less, the agency said Friday.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Oraclum Hedge Fund Founder Charged With Lying About Returns
item.description: Vuk Vukovic, a founder of New York hedge fund Oraclum Capital LLC, was charged by federal prosecutors with lying to investors about his fund’s performance.
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris and Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Dollar Wavers as CPI Adds to Fed Hike Bets While Oil Falls
item.description: The dollar oscillated Friday after a key gauge of US consumer prices rose by more than expected, pushing traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova

item.title: Treasuries End Bruising Week With Fed Hike Bets Firmed After CPI
item.description: The $32 trillion US bond market ended a bruising week that pushed yields to multiyear highs, with investors more convinced the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to address sticky inflation.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie and Greg Ritchie

item.title: Lululemon’s Newest Bear Sees More Pain Ahead After 81% Rout
item.description: Lululemon Athletica Inc.’s turnaround won’t be a quick or easy fix as the athletic wear company cedes market share to rivals and suffers deepening sales declines, according to BMO Capital Markets, which initiated coverage of the stock this week with an underperform rating.
item.dc:creator: Peyton Forte

item.title: Stocks Climb in Run-Up to Next Week’s Fed Decision: Markets Wrap
item.description: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks rising, with a decline in oil prices tempering concerns about inflationary pressures ahead of next week’s Federal Reserve decision.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth
